To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

disruption of NUDT-2, a gene that encodes an enzyme which degrades the nucleotide Ap4A, leads to increased levels of this metabolite and that Ap4A down-regulates genes involved in immune response and tumor promotion and up-regulates genes involved tumor suppression.
NUDT2 is a novel anti-cancer target that exerts its effects by regulating gene expression.
NUDT2 gene disruption elevates intracellular Ap4a and down-regulates immune response and cancer promotion genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new targets for cancer chemotherapy.
the regulation of gene expression in response to changes in intracellular Ap 4A concentration.
the role of the NUDT family of proteins in the regulation of cell signaling and gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NUDT2 and Ap4A are involved in a complex and multifaceted network of cellular processes that are critical for maintaining homeostasis in the cell and that disruption of NUDT and Ap4A can have significant effects on the cell and its environment.
Ap4A is a novel regulator of gene expression, with a major role in the suppression of immune response and cancer promotion genes.
Ap4A is a negative modulator of gene transcription and that NUDT2 plays an important role in the regulation of the immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NUDTI gene product, a protein that hydrolyzes Ap4A, is required to suppress the expression of a wide variety of immune and cancer-promoting genes.
the Nudt2 gene is a potential tumor promoter and that its disruption may provide a novel therapeutic target for cancer.
the NUDt2 gene is essential for the normal immune system and that disruption of this gene is a potential cancer chemotherapeutic strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the NUDTs are a novel class of cancer chemotherapeutic targets that are highly conserved in humans and other species and are likely to be involved in the regulation of multiple pathways that are important to the development and progression of cancer.

the NUDTI2 gene is involved in the regulation of a large number of genes that are involved in immune responses, inflammation and tumor promotion and that the loss of NUDT function leads to the up-regulation of genes involved in immune responses and tumor promotion.
Ap4A has a significant effect on gene expression, and the effect appears to be anti-tumor.
